# Configuration

<!-- Generated by tools/release/gen_configuration_doc.py from src/ini_public.h. Do not edit by hand. -->

Redemption Editor reads `RedemptionEditor.ini` in the game folder (next to `RDR2.exe`) when the game starts. When the file is missing, the mod writes it with the text below (the same file as `dist/RedemptionEditor.ini`). Every value in it is the default: a key you delete reads the same value.

> Redemption Editor settings. Lines that start with ";" are comments. Every value below is the default: delete a line and the mod uses the same value. The mod reads this file when the game starts.

## [RedemptionEditor]

Recording, clips, the world state, logging and reports. The commented lines at the end are the editor's own preferences: the editor writes them when you change them in its menus.

| Key | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `Language` | `auto` | The language of the editor and its notices: auto (the game's language) or one of en, pt-BR, es, es-MX, fr, de, it, pl, ru, ja, ko, zh-CN, zh-TW (a file of the RedemptionEditor\lang folder, without .lang). |
| `ReplayBuffer` | `1` | The replay buffer: the mod always records the last seconds around you while nothing plays; the SaveBuffer key saves them as a clip. 1 on, 0 off. |
| `ReplayBufferSeconds` | `60` | How many seconds the buffer keeps (10 or more). |
| `ReplayBufferMB` | `128` | The buffer's memory in MB (16 or more). In busy places (Saint Denis) the buffer may keep fewer seconds than asked; the save tells you when it does. The buffer's seconds and memory do not limit a manual recording. 16 to 960 (a saved buffer stays under the 1 GiB a clip file may hold). |

Manual recording (the Record key starts and stops it), with the buffer on or off. A long recording is saved in parts, each its own clip (names ending in -p1, -p2...): a part closes at ManualMaxMB (32 to 960; a busy town fills 900 MB in 2 to 3 minutes) or after ManualMaxSeconds (0: no time limit), a notice says so, and the recording goes on in the next part. With the buffer on, a part also holds up to ReplayBufferMB when that is larger.

| Key | Default |
|---|---|
| `ManualMaxSeconds` | `0` |
| `ManualMaxMB` | `900` |

Clips are saved compressed. Clips you have not opened for CompressAfterDays days are compressed further in the background (they still open in the editor). Level 1 (fast) to 22 (smallest).

| Key | Default |
|---|---|
| `CompressClips` | `1` |
| `CompressAfterDays` | `1` |
| `CompressLevel` | `19` |

Cutscenes: 0 pauses the recording while a cutscene plays, 1 records it. LockCutsceneCamera=1: camera markers inside a recorded cutscene keep the game's camera. Both are also in the editor's Replay Settings.

| Key | Default |
|---|---|
| `RecordCutscenes` | `0` |
| `LockCutsceneCamera` | `0` |

| Key | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `ReplayDeadEye` | `0` | 1: the Dead Eye look is played back with the clip (Replay Settings). |
| `FreezeWorldOnPause` | `1` | 1: the world stays frozen while a replay is paused (Replay Settings). |
| `RecordingIndicator` | `normal` | The REC notice while you record (Replay Settings): normal; brief (3 seconds when a recording starts, stops or saves); hidden (you see it, screen recorders such as OBS, NVIDIA and Game Bar do not; Windows 10 2004 or newer and the game windowed or borderless, else it works as brief); off. |
| `InterfaceScale` | `100` | The size of the editor's menus, panels, texts and notices, in percent (Replay Settings): 80, 90, 100, 110 or 125. 100 looks the same at every resolution. A 4:3 screen stays at 100 at most. |
| `RestoreWorldState` | `1` | The map state of the clip (doors, buildings and other world pieces of the place where it was recorded) is put back while it plays. 0: only a notice. |
| `RestoreWorldStateInMission` | `0` | 1: also while a mission runs (by default a mission's world is left alone). |
| `FullLog` | `1` | Logging. 1 writes the full log (RedemptionEditor.log), what we need when you report a problem; 0 keeps only the essential lines (a smaller file). |
| `QaMarks` | `1` | Reports. The MarkProblem key marks a problem while a replay plays (QaMarks=1), the Report key saves a report ZIP in the ReplayReports folder (see the README). |
| `ReportIncludeClips` | `0` | The report ZIP carries the clips you marked and no other. 1 also adds the clip open in the editor. |

## [Export]

| Key | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `Enabled` | `1` | Video export (Ctrl+E in the clip editor). 1 on, 0 off. Needs the game on Vulkan; on DirectX 12 the export refuses to start. |
| `Folder` | (empty) | Where videos go. Empty: Documents\Rockstar Games\Red Dead Redemption 2\Videos\Redemption Editor |
| `Encoder` | `auto` | The video encoder: auto, nvenc, amf, qsv or cpu. |
| `Hdr10` | `0` | 1: HDR10 video. |
| `Lut` | (empty) | A .cube colour LUT applied to the export (a full path). Empty: none. |
| `AudioOffsetMs` | `140` | How many ms the game's sound is moved earlier in the video, so shots land on their muzzle flash. |

## [Keys]

The keys of every action. The free camera's movement keys (W A S D, Q E, Z C, the arrows, Page Up and Page Down, Shift and Ctrl) and the editor's own keys (Esc, Enter, Backspace, Space, Tab, Del, Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y, Ctrl+E, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, F1) are fixed.

Every action's keys (the defaults below): one or two keys separated by a comma, with Shift+ or Ctrl+ in front (Shift+F4). Empty or None: no key. The editor's texts and its F1 key list show the keys set here.

| Key | Default | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `PlayPause` | `K` | Play, pause |
| `FrameBack` | `Comma` | One frame back (hold: rewind) |
| `FrameForward` | `Period` | One frame forward (hold: fast forward) |
| `Rewind` | (empty) | Rewind while held |
| `FastForward` | (empty) | Fast forward while held |
| `SpeedDown` | `LeftBracket` | Slower playback |
| `SpeedUp` | `RightBracket` | Faster playback |
| `FreeCam` | `F11` | Free camera |
| `HideUi` | `H` | Hide the replay UI (the keys keep working) |
| `Editor` | `F2` | Open, close the editor |
| `Stop` | `F7` | Play / stop the last clip |
| `Record` | `F4` | Record / mark a recording |
| `SaveBuffer` | `Shift+F4` | Save the replay buffer |
| `MarkProblem` | `Shift+F2` | Mark a problem (QA report) |
| `Report` | `Shift+F1` | Save the QA report (one zip, every mark and its clips) |
| `FreeCamDrone` | `V` | Free camera: Drone flight (momentum, banking) on/off |
| `FreeCamAcrobatic` | `N` | Free camera: acrobatic rotation (full rolls and loops) on/off |
| `FreeCamWalk` | `B` | Free camera: Walk (the ground at eye height) on/off |
| `FreeCamCollision` | `Y` | Free camera: collision with the world on/off |
| `FreeCamLockAltitude` | `U` | Free camera: keep the altitude on/off |
| `FreeCamFollow` | `F` | Free camera: follow the target (rigid, position only, off) |
| `FreeCamPick` | `G` | Free camera: the target under the crosshair |
| `FreeCamPickNearest` | `Shift+G` | Free camera: the nearest target |
| `FreeCamLevel` | `Num5` | Free camera: level the horizon |
| `FreeCamBehind` | `Num0` | Free camera: behind the main character |
| `FreeCamLock` | `L` | Free camera: hold still on/off |
| `CameraOverlay` | `Backquote` | Camera markers and path in the world on/off |

## Where the mod writes

Everything the mod writes goes to one base folder: the game folder when the mod can write there, else `Documents\Rockstar Games\Red Dead Redemption 2\Redemption Editor`, else `%LOCALAPPDATA%\RedemptionEditor`. In the base folder:

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Clips and their thumbnails | `ReplayClips\` |
| Projects | `ReplayProjects\` |
| Report ZIPs and problem marks | `ReplayReports\` |
| Developer reports | `ReplayDebug\` |
| The log and the crash log | `RedemptionEditor.log`, `RedemptionEditor.crash.log` |
| The settings you change in the editor (only when the base is not the game folder) | `RedemptionEditor.ini` |

Crash dumps always go to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\RedemptionEditor\crashes`, and exported videos to `Documents\Rockstar Games\Red Dead Redemption 2\Videos\Redemption Editor` (`[Export] Folder` moves them).

**A game in Program Files.** Windows does not let a game that runs without administrator rights write to `C:\Program Files` or `C:\Program Files (x86)` (the Rockstar Games Launcher's default, and Steam's). At start the mod writes, reopens and deletes a test file in the game folder and in each data folder above; when one of them is refused (or Windows quietly redirects the write to its VirtualStore), the base is the Documents folder. You don't need to change any folder permissions. Clips and projects already in the game folder still show in the gallery and open; a clip or project you change is saved to the base folder under the same name. The `RedemptionEditor.ini` of the game folder is still read, and the settings you change in the editor go to the base folder's `RedemptionEditor.ini`, whose keys win. If no folder takes writes, a notice says where saving failed and why. The log line `STORAGE_BASE` names the base and the reason.

## Advanced switches

Advanced switches exist for support; we'll tell you if you need one. They are not in the file, and every one is on by default. If an issue or a crash report reply asks you to add one, put the line it gives you under `[RedemptionEditor]` and restart the game.

## Developer keys

The public build reads only the keys above and the advanced switches. A developer build (`/p:RedemptionDev=true`, see [building.md](building.md)) also reads the research and tuning keys; see [release/ini-and-dev-build.md](release/ini-and-dev-build.md).
